info.text:
The US has exported more petroleum than it imports every year since 2020, yet regular gas averaged about $4.47 a gallon on September 28, 2026. This video follows one barrel of oil from the Strait of Hormuz to your receipt: why oil has one world price, the history from the 1973 embargo to 2026, the simple rule that every $1 on a barrel adds about 2.4 cents to a gallon, and how the shock spreads into record diesel, airfares up 23.4%, plastic packaging and fertilizer. With real math on a 15-gallon fill-up.

0:00 Intro
0:46 One world price
2:26 We've been here before
3:46 Ripple one: the pump
6:05 Ripple two: trucks and planes
7:36 Ripple three: plastics, food
9:36 Recap

Sources: EIA weekly gasoline and diesel prices (Sept 21-28, 2026); EIA monthly and annual retail gasoline prices (2020-2026); EIA, What we pay for in a gallon of gasoline (2025); EIA Strait of Hormuz analysis (2024 data); EIA US petroleum trade (2025); BLS Consumer Price Index, August 2026 (released Sept 11, 2026); AAA (Sept 2026); CNBC (Apr 21 and Sept 29, 2026); Bloomberg and Forbes (Apr 7, 2026); IATA Global Outlook for Air Transport (June 2026); World Bank (Apr 2026); ICIS (Apr 14, 2026); Canada Energy Regulator (2025); China customs data (2025); Argus/METI (2025); Federal Reserve History, Oil Shock of 1973-74; CFTC (Apr 2020).

News and education, not financial advice.
